# Generation 2 Code-First Delta

The Awtsmoos gave the planned sitemap a deeper face; Awtsmoos.com now carries semantic truth into each registered static world before the browser begins its race.

## Planned versus actual

- Planned: central app/game metadata enrichment.
  - Actual: 75 registry-backed app/game documents plus four curated public-information documents, 79 total generated metadata records.
- Planned: enrich translation titles when authoritative metadata exists.
  - Actual: corpus manifests and bundle payloads contain stable coordinates but no trustworthy human title field, so no title invention was allowed.
- Planned: richer alias discovery.
  - Actual: validated alias SSR now contains a bounded authored-post section backed by existing authorship-verifying profile machinery, limited to 12 posts.
- Planned: deliberate public-family coverage.
  - Actual: About, Docs, Social, and Contact entered core discovery; Donate and action/auth/control surfaces remain excluded for lack of semantic/public-content evidence.
- Planned: native comment future-proofing.
  - Actual: comment sitemap logic gained an injected pure factory and deterministic tests for roots, replies, deleted/malformed pointers, and stale aliases.

## Runtime-discovered corrections

- Extensionless app/game registry hrefs originally canonicalized to redirecting URLs. Directory canonicals now normalize to the final slash URL.
- Apostrophes inside authored meta descriptions exposed a quote-fragile build parser. Static metadata extraction is now quote-aware and entity-aware.
- A runtime verifier repeated the old apostrophe parsing mistake. Quote-aware verification proved the served Docs description is complete.

## Shadow work discovered

- OpenGraph title should prefer an authored document title when present rather than a shorter registry fallback.
- Registry-backed public pages can carry minimal JSON-LD structured data without changing visible application UI.
- Current real alias data contains zero authored-post records among six public aliases; deterministic tests preserve future behavior until real data appears.
